description: Kolossi Castle contains a documented painted Crucifixion. This record concerns the wall painting within the historic building rather than a separate movable museum collection.

description: This Galata church, dedicated to the Mother of God and also known as Archangel Michael, was painted by Simeon Axentis. Its programme extends from Mary’s childhood to the Resurrection.

name: Holy Cross (Stavros) tou Agiasmati, Platanistasa
description: The Holy Cross church near Platanistasa contains Philip Goul’s signed decoration and a detailed cycle of the Cross. Some sanctuary paintings are attributed to Minas; the dating of the main ensemble remains disputed.

name: Panagia Chrysokourdaliotissa, Kourdali
description: The three-aisled church at Kourdali contains an anonymous painted ensemble. Sanctuary imagery, Marian narratives and devotional saints include a figure identified as Luke by the opening words of his Gospel.

name: Saint Mamas, Louvaras
description: Dedicated to Saint Mamas, this church at Louvaras contains Philip Goul’s wall paintings. Its programme includes the Hospitality of Abraham, the Washing of the Feet and an extensive Passion sequence.

name: Transfiguration, Palaichori
description: The Transfiguration church at Palaichori contains an early sixteenth-century ensemble by an unnamed painter, attributed to Philip Goul by Eliades. Later paintings on the exterior western wall are dated 1612.

name: Panagia Kanakaria, Lythrangomi
description: Panagia Kanakaria at Lythrangomi combines an early Christian architectural history with later rebuilding and painting. The wall paintings catalogued here are distinct from the church’s better-known early apse mosaics.

name: Panagia, Trikomo
description: A wall painting is recorded at Panagia, Trikomo. Christ is represented within an almond-shaped glory surrounded by four angels.

description: Saint George of the Greeks is the ruined Greek cathedral of Famagusta. Its sanctuary paintings connect biblical narrative with liturgy; later scholarship has revised the dating and interpretation of particular registers.

name: Old Archbishopric, ground floor, Nicosia

name: Saints Kerykos and Julitta, Letymbou
